title: Every job
subtitle: The job process, the never list, PPE, what to do if something goes wrong, and the free service period.
source: LPC Tech Onboarding Pack: job process, never list, PPE requirements, if something goes wrong, free service period

sections.heading: The job process: every job, every time
sections.body: Follow this process on every job without exception. It is what separates a professional service from an average one.

sections.title: 1. Before leaving
items: Check the Job Calendar: confirm job details, address & any customer notes
Vehicle stocked with correct chemicals & equipment for this job type
SMS or call customer with ETA if running late

sections.title: 2. On arrival
items: Park professionally (do not block driveways or neighbours)
PPE on before entering
Greet customer: introduce yourself by name
Ask customer to point out hot spots or problem areas
Briefly explain what you'll be doing before you start

sections.title: 3. During treatment
items: Take BEFORE photos of hot spot areas
Follow the field guide for this job type, no shortcuts
Apply per product label, never exceed rates
Keep chemicals away from food, children and pets
Note any areas you cannot treat and why

sections.title: 4. After treatment
items: Take AFTER photos
Brief customer on re-entry time (1 to 2 hours once dry) [Mitch to confirm: the CAS, cockroach, ant and spider guides tell the customer about an hour once dry]
Tell customer what to expect: may see more activity for 2 to 3 weeks, that's normal
Explain the free service period (internal 6 months, external 3 months)
Ask for a Google review: do it now, while they're happy. Mitch also sends the review link again 5 days after the job, so you don't need to chase it
Leave service report or confirm it's being emailed

sections.title: 5. End of day
items: Log job with chemical usage in reporting system [Mitch to confirm which system]
Send invoice if not already provided
Note any follow-up required and tell Mitch
Restock vehicle if anything is low
Update Mitch on anything unusual from the day

items.text: Never mix chemicals without checking the label first
Never apply chemicals without appropriate PPE

items.detail: More is not better and it's illegal

items.text: Never quote termite treatments, barriers or complex jobs
items.detail: These always go to Mitch, too many variables

items.text: Never discuss pricing on complex jobs
items.detail: Say "Mitch will get back to you with a quote"
Follow SDS procedure and call Mitch immediately

items.text: Never use the vehicle for personal use
Never post about jobs or customers on social media

sections.heading: PPE requirements
rows: Gloves and closed shoes at minimum on every job
Gloves, mask, eye protection as per product SDS
Dust mask, gloves, torch, appropriate footwear
Gloves at all times when handling traps or bait
Coveralls, gloves, mask. Change before entering next property.

sections.body: Never apply chemicals without PPE. If the SDS requires it, you wear it. No exceptions.

sections.heading: If something goes wrong
rows: Listen, stay calm, do not argue. Tell them Mitch will call them today. Call Mitch immediately.
Stop immediately. Do not continue. Call Mitch.
Follow SDS procedure. Call Mitch immediately.
Ensure safety. Call 000 if needed. Then call Mitch.
Treat injury first. Call Mitch. Document what happened.
Stay calm. Remove yourself. Call Mitch.

sections.title: Call Mitch
sections.body: 0432 181 689. After hours or urgent, call Mitch directly.

sections.heading: Free service period
sections.body: We call it a free service period, not a warranty. If a customer is not happy, we go back. Customer satisfaction comes first, always.

rows: No free service period. Inspection only, not a guarantee.
Be lenient. If a customer calls with an issue, we go back. It costs less than losing a customer or a bad review.
Tell Mitch. He will decide whether to send you back or attend himself.

sections.body: Never tell a customer their issue is not covered without checking with Mitch first.
